rule: Only exact-head real compiler/runtime execution may set verified_compiled=true. Host/reference models and zero-step workflows never do.

evidence_notes.overflow_error_abi: Staged semantics are not compiled verification. Java has a guest ArithmeticOverflowError object with Error-root matching but explicit source throw/raise/panic remains closed. LLVM has terminal checked-overflow catch plus an allocation-free cross-frame i64 effect-result ABI, but ordinary call lowering still returns scalar i64 and uncaught overflow still traps. .NET normalizes CLR overflow to Throw/65537 in OresIR and emitted-CIL verification, while production generated CIL still uses CLR checked-exception transport until a guest handler frame is emitted. Forge has Throw/65537 in the checked interpreter and an opt-in effect-aware x86-64/AArch64 register ABI; its no-handler native emitter still traps. None of these staged bridges establish full source catch/raise/panic parity.
